title: VideoScout: Learning Agentic Active Exploration with Adaptive Reasoning Pacing for Long Video Understanding
abstract: arXiv:2609.15606v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have achieved remarkable progress on short video understanding yet remain limited on long videos due to the limited visual context window. Prevailing approaches rely on uniform frame sampling or recent coarse-to-fine agentic zooming, both of which struggle to localize sparse, decisive evidence in sufficiently long videos. We formulate long video understanding as a \textbf{Sequential Evidence Acquisition (SEA)} problem, in which an agent reads the video turn by turn along the temporal axis, deciding at each turn how fast to watch, what evidence to retain, when to revisit uncertain segments, and when to stop and answer. Inspired by this view, we propose \textbf{VideoScout}, a multi-turn reasoning agent that instantiates the SEA paradigm through adaptive reasoning pacing. translated_title: VideoScout：通过自适应推理节奏学习智能体主动探索以实现长视频理解
translated_abstract: 多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）在短视频理解方面已取得显著进展，但由于视觉上下文窗口的有限性，其在长视频理解上仍存在局限。主流方法依赖于均匀帧采样或近期的粗到细智能体缩放策略，这两种方法都难以在足够长的视频中定位稀疏但具有决定性的证据。我们将长视频理解形式化为一个序贯证据获取问题，其中一个智能体沿时间轴逐轮读取视频，在每一轮决定观看速度、保留哪些证据、何时重访不确定的片段，以及何时停止并给出回答。受这一观点启发，我们提出了VideoScout，一个通过自适应推理节奏来实例化SEA范式的多轮推理智能体。具体而言，通过动态控制观看节奏，VideoScout能够在有限的预算内高效遍历长视频……
tldr: 该论文提出VideoScout，一种基于序贯证据获取（SEA）范式的多轮推理智能体，通过自适应推理节奏动态控制观看速度、证据保留与重访决策，从而在有限预算内高效定位长视频中的关键决定性证据。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes VideoScout, a multi-turn reasoning agent that instantiates the Sequential Evidence Acquisition (SEA) paradigm through adaptive reasoning pacing, dynamically deciding viewing speed, evidence retention, and when to revisit uncertain segments, enabling efficient localization of sparse decisive evidence in long videos within a bounded budget.
